resources.string: Add the desktop running CodeCockpit, then pair with the secret from its Settings → Remote access tab.
Remove "%s"? The stored token for this desktop is deleted too.
An address shown on the desktop, e.g. 192.168.1.20
IPv6 address shown on the desktop, e.g. [2408:8256::1]
Fill in an address and the pairing secret.
This desktop is already in the list.
First connection to %1$s. Compare this fingerprint with the one shown in CodeCockpit → Settings → Remote access, then trust it.
Certificate fingerprint changed for %1$s. This can mean a reinstall — or someone intercepting the connection. Connection refused.

Cannot reach %1$s. Check that the phone can reach the desktop (same network, or a tunnel app such as Tailscale on both), that remote access is enabled in CodeCockpit, and that the firewall allows the port.
Pairing was revoked on the desktop. Enter the secret again to pair.
Too many failed attempts — wait a minute and try again.
The desktop already serves the maximum number of remote clients.
The desktop is not reachable right now — check that CodeCockpit is running with remote access enabled, and that the device ID is correct.
Start a session in CodeCockpit on the desktop — it appears here live.
Send a prompt to the agent…
This session has exited on the desktop.
Bypass mode lets the agent run any command without asking for approval. Enable it?
The companion app for CodeCockpit. Watch your AI coding sessions — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode — and drive them from your phone.
Enable Remote access on the desktop
Turn it on and copy the pairing secret
Windows asks for firewall access the first time — accept it
Add the desktop — with an address and the secret, or just its device ID and the secret
Same network: any address shown on the desktop works. IPv6 direct: the public IPv6 address — also across the internet when both ends have IPv6.
On first connect, compare the certificate fingerprint with the one shown on the desktop
Address: any one listed in CodeCockpit → Settings → Remote access — the local network one, or one from a tunnel app such as Tailscale.
IPv6 address: one listed under “IPv6 direct” in CodeCockpit → Settings → Remote access, brackets included, e.g. [2408:8256::1].
Port: shown in the same place. The default is 47315.
Pairing secret: copy it from that tab. It never leaves your devices.
Paste the pairing secret from the desktop.
Show or hide the pairing secret
The phone connects to the desktop directly. Any address listed under Settings → Remote access works — the local one, or one from a tunnel app such as Tailscale.
On the desktop, pick “IPv6 direct” under Settings → Remote access and copy an address. Enter it here with the pairing secret — it works across the internet whenever both ends have IPv6.
This network probably has no IPv6 (cellular data usually does, Wi-Fi often does not). You can still try.
Require the phone’s screen lock — fingerprint, face, or PIN — before opening this app.
No screen lock is set up on this device. Add one in Android settings first.
You are on the latest version.
Could not reach GitHub. Check your connection.
Version %1$s was published on GitHub. You are on %2$s.
Select a session from the sidebar, or start a new one.
Absolute path on the desktop, e.g. D:/work/app
Close “%s”? The agent process on the desktop is terminated.
No history for this engine yet
Delete “%s” from history? The record is removed on the desktop permanently.
